payload.task: self_diffusion of Li+ in pristine crystalline LiF by MD (units cm2/s)
payload.reason: Premise check failed: the requested quantity is not measurable with direct MD on a pristine crystal. (1) Li transport in crystalline LiF is defect-mediated (vacancies/interstitials). A pristine periodic supercell has no defects, and thermally creating a Schottky or Frenkel defect costs several eV. At any temperature below the melting point (~1121 K), the expected equilibrium number of defects in a 10^3-10^4 atom cell is << 1. So an MLIP/classical MD run lasting ns shows only vibrational MSD (a plateau of ~0.1 A^2). The resulting 'D' is zero to within noise. That reflects the defect-free cell, not the physical value. (2) Detection floor: with MSD noise of ~0.1 A^2 over about 1-10 ns, MD can only resolve D above roughly 1e-9 to 1e-8 cm2/s. The real lattice diffusivity of solid LiF is many orders of magnitude below this at ordinary temperatures. Near melting it is still set by extrinsic and thermal defect concentrations that a pristine cell cannot represent. (3) The measured D in real LiF is controlled by impurity (aliovalent) content and processing history (extrinsic regime), so no single 'pristine' number exists to validate against. Forcing hopping by superheating above Tm would melt the cell and give a liquid diffusivity, not a crystal one. Any number I posted would therefore be either a noise-level upper bound or an artifact. I have not posted a property_result.

details.premise_check: failed - property is defect-controlled and below the MD resolution floor; a pristine cell gives D = 0 (artifact)
details.calibration_data: /data/calibration/tier1.json contains no LiF record, so no independent measured anchor was available
well_posed_alternatives: Defect-explicit route: add a known Li vacancy concentration (e.g. 1 V_Li plus a charge-compensating F vacancy or a divalent substituent) and run NVT MD at several T between about 800 and 1050 K. Get D_vac*c_vac from MSD (Einstein relation, block-averaged), fit an Arrhenius law, and report D as a function of stated vacancy concentration. This gives the vacancy-mediated (extrinsic-type) diffusivity with its assumptions explicit.

Barrier route: compute the Li-vacancy migration barrier (NEB/static or MD-hopping rate) and the Schottky formation energy with the same model. Then D(T) = (1/6) z a^2 nu exp(-(Ef/2 + Em)/kT) for the intrinsic regime, with the uncertainty propagated from the barrier errors.
Upper-bound route: run pristine-cell MD near (below) Tm and report only an upper bound D < MSD_noise/(6t), explicitly flagged as a resolution limit, not a value.

Validation for any of these: reproduce the LiF melting point (~1121 K) or the lattice constant and thermal expansion with the same MLIP, and compare the migration barrier or the high-T conductivity with measured ionic-conductivity data for LiF before trusting D.
